news.title: 马斯克关闭xAI内幕：SpaceX AI崛起，2万亿美元IPO估值战对抗Anthropic升温
news.snippet: 马斯克宣布解散xAI并将其并入SpaceX，引发与Anthropic的AI估值竞争。
news.raw_snippet: Elon Musk announced the dissolution of xAI, merging it into SpaceX and rebranding it as "SpaceX AI." This move is widely seen as paving the way for SpaceX's historic initial public offering (IPO), with market estimates valuing SpaceX at up to $2 trillion. Concurrently, xAI's core computing asset—the Colossus 1 data center housing over 220,000 Nvidia GPUs—has been entirely leased to rival Anthropic, which recently signed major computing deals with Akamai and Google, seeing its pre-IPO valuation surge to $1.2 trillion. All 12 of xAI's original co-founders have departed, and the Grok model's performance lags behind GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.7, highlighting the "kill zone" pressure facing closed-source models. Billionaire Elon Musk recently announced the dissolution of his artificial intelligence company, xAI, merging it into his space exploration company, SpaceX, under the new name "SpaceX AI." This move is not merely an internal corporate restructuring but a strategic step to clear the path for SpaceX's historic initial public offering (IPO).

news.raw_snippet: Michael Burry Expands AI Short as 2026 IPO Wave Tests Bubble Warning. Michael Burry, the investor known for predicting the 2008 housing-market collapse, has expanded his bearish bet against artificial intelligence-linked stocks. That filing showed major put positions against Palantir and Nvidia as of September 30, 2025. Data compiled from the filing showed Scion held about $912.1 million in notional Palantir puts. However, Michael Burry’s newest comments suggest the trade is no longer limited to high valuations. That marks a sharper challenge to one of the most visible AI software names in public markets. OpenAI, for instance, has been laying the groundwork for a potential IPO at a valuation of up to $1 trillion. In December, the company was preparing for a possible IPO as early as 2026. His expanded short positions turn the 2026 IPO pipeline into a major test of market confidence, valuation discipline, and the durability of the AI boom.

news.snippet: Cerebras启动零售路演获Sam Altman背书，AI芯片企业上市进程加速，投资者需关注技术壁垒。
news.raw_snippet: Cerebras' retail roadshow featured an endorsement from Sam Altman chief of OpenAI, one of the chipmaker's customers. Investors may be fixated on some of the highest-profile names, such as OpenAI and Anthropic. Cerebras on Monday re-submitted its initial public offering documents with the Securities and Exchange Commission—it initially filed in October, then withdrew—aiming to sell 28 million shares at a price between $115 and $125 apiece.At the high end of that range, Cerebras' IPO would raise some $3.5 billion, and its implied market capitalization would be over $26 billion. There's a growing line of private AI companies looking to go public, and that doesn't just mean expected mega offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic. Those listings will shed new light on the inner workings of the AI sector, and could offer more opportunity and options for investors too. Cerebras' retail roadshow featured an endorsement from Sam Altman, founder of OpenAI, which Cerebras counts as a customer and partner.

news.raw_snippet: OpenAI logo on a smartphone. ## Qualcomm CEO Says OpenAI, Meta Are Working On AI Wearables That Could Replace Smartphones. **Qualcomm Inc.**(NASDAQ:QCOM) CEO says the smartphone era may be nearing its end as major artificial intelligence companies quietly work on next-generation wearable devices powered by advanced AI agents. Amon described a future centered on what he calls an "ecosystem of you," where devices such as glasses, earbuds and pins continuously collect context from users and allow AI agents to perform tasks automatically. "If AI understands what we say, what we hear, what we see… all of this information is going to be very important context for agents to do things for you," he said. On Wednesday, Qualcomm Chief Executive **Cristiano Amon** said the company is collaborating with "pretty much all" leading AI players, including **OpenAI** and **Meta Platforms** **Inc.** (NASDAQ:META). OpenAI is reportedly developing an AI agent smartphone with Qualcomm and MediaTek, aiming to replace apps with task-driven AI by 2028.
